test.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids - Test 5
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: In a hydraulic lift, the surface area of the input piston is \(6 \mathrm{~cm}^2\) and that of the output piston is \(1500 \mathrm{~cm}^2\). If 100 N force is applied to the input piston to raise the output piston by 20 cm, then the work done is _______ kJ.

The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The velocity of water is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>V</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is _________.

There is an air bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> in a liquid of surface tension <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>075</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> below the free surface. The amount by which the pressure inside the bubble is greater than the atmospheric pressure is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>.

A small spherical ball of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> falls freely under gravity through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> will be ____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, viscosity of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>‐</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ).

In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>70</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>65</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. If the wing area is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the lift of the wing is _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. (Given density of air <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>64</mn></math> identical drops each charged upto potential of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mV</mi></math> are combined to form a bigger drop. The potential of the bigger drop will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mV</mi></math>.

The diameter of an air bubble which was initially <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)

A liquid of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> flows smoothly through a horizontal pipe that tapers in cross-sectional area from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of the pipe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></math>. The rate of flow of liquid is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

A metal block of base area 0.20 m2 is placed on a table, as shown in figure. A liquid film of thickness 0.25 mm is inserted between the block and the table. The block is pushed by a horizontal force of 0.1 N and moves with a constant speed. If the viscosity of the liquid is 5.0×10–3 Pl, the speed of block is ______ ×10-3 m s-1.

A soap bubble of the radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is formed inside another soap bubble of radius, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The radius of an equivalent soap bubble that has the same excess pressure as inside the smaller bubble with respect to the atmospheric pressure is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

The velocity of upper layer of water in a river is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Shearing stress between horizontal layers of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Depth of the river is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. (Co-efficient of viscosity of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>)
A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of 1000 droplets to that of energy of big drop is $\frac{10}{x}$. The value of $x$ is __________

Small water droplets of radius $0.01 \mathrm{~mm}$ are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Due to condensation, if 8 such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be _____$\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$.

The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is $n$ times the volume of the bubble $B$, then, the value of $n$ is ___.

An air bubble of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> rises steadily through a solution of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> at the rate of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>35</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The co-efficient of viscosity of the solution (neglect density of air) is ________ Pas (given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).

A soap bubble is blown to a diameter of $7 \mathrm{~cm} .36960 \mathrm{erg}$ of work is done in blowing it further. If surface tension of soap solution is $40 \mathrm{dyne} / \mathrm{cm}$ then the new radius is______ $\mathrm{cm}$ Take $\left(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\right)$

Suppose you have taken a dilute solution of oleic acid in such a way that its concentration becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of oleic acid per <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of the solution. Then you make a thin film of this solution (monomolecular thickness) of area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> by considering <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> spherical drops of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>40</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Then the thickness of oleic acid layer will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ________ .

A spherical drop of liquid splits into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> identical spherical drops. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> is the surface energy of the original drop and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, the (ignoring evaporation), <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">u</mi><mi mathvariant="italic">f</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="italic">u</mi><mi mathvariant="italic">i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mfenced></math>. Then value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______:

An air bubble of radius 1.0 mm is observed at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid having surface tension $0.095 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^2$ and density $10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. The difference between pressure inside the bubble and atmospheric pressure is _____ $\mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^2$. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )

The surface tension of soap solution is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The amount of work done required to increase the radius of soap bubble from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> . (take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>)
